question: Does GRPO's group size (num_generations) move held-out accuracy, when every arm is held to the same rollout budget so bigger groups do not simply buy more compute?
method: LoRA GRPO (r=16, alpha=32, lr 5e-6, beta 0.04, scale_rewards=True, temp 0.8), TRL GRPOTrainer
metric: pass@1 on 100 held-out GSM8K test questions, graded by wai.verify.MathEqual() (a program, not a judge)

budget_control.held_fixed: steps x generation_batch = 48 x 16 = 768 rollouts per arm
budget_control.note: the shipped GRPO recipe sets per_device_train_batch_size=num_generations, which makes G cost 4x more at G=8 than at G=2; here the generation batch is pinned at 16 instead
budget_control.check: all three arms completed 48 steps within seconds of each other on identical hardware

eval.decontamination_result: 384 train prompts in, 384 kept, 0 contaminated (GSM8K train/test are disjoint; a clean control, not a save)
eval.powered_for_source: holdout_size(0.10, base=0.45, k=4) -> 98 tasks; +0.05 would need 391
eval.training_reward_note: both are MathEqual on the final answer, on purpose: any gap between arms is the knob, not reward design. This run therefore says nothing about reward hacking.

noise_floor.rule: t(df=2)=4.30 x run_std x sqrt(1/1 + 1/1), from compare(run_std=, run_std_runs=3)

headline: Group size did not move held-out GSM8K pass@1 at a fixed 768-rollout budget; every paired interval contains zero and sits inside the 0.063 noise band. One level down the knob moved decisively: the share of unanimous (zero-advantage) groups fell 0.693 -> 0.448 -> 0.281, but at G=8 that is 19x the 0.015 an iid model predicts, because GSM8K at this model size is mostly saturated prompts rather than borderline ones. That prices dynamic sampling at ~28% of the budget reclaimed instead of ~1.5%.
limitations: 48 steps is about one pass over 384 prompts; training reward showed no trend and KL stayed near zero, so the arms were never likely to separate on the metric at this budget
30-35% of completions hit the 320-token cap and a truncated answer scores zero, depressing every pass rate (equal across arms, so the comparison survives)
one seed per arm; the noise floor is across containers, not across training seeds
powered for +0.10 only; effects smaller than that are unresolved, not absent
